# Backend parity

What each `Store` backend implements, declared by the backend itself (see
`crates/store/src/capabilities.rs`). **full** = the conformance suite runs the surface's
complete semantics against it. **refused** = every method of that surface answers
`StoreError::Unsupported`, which the API renders as HTTP 501 `unsupported` — and the
conformance suite asserts that refusal, so a gap can never quietly become an empty page.

| Surface | sqlite | postgres | firestore |
|---|---|---|---|
| `events_core` | full | full | full |
| `event_filters` | full | full | full |
| `rollup` | full | full | full |
| `traces` | full | full | refused |
| `forecast` | full | full | full |
| `margin_breakdowns` | full | full | full |
| `prompts` | full | refused | full |
| `relay` | full | full | refused |
| `collective` | full | refused | refused |
| `project_admin` | full | full | refused |
| `key_admin` | full | full | full |
| `limit_lifecycle` | full | full | full |
| `job_leases` | full | full | full |
| `maintenance` | full | refused | refused |
| `metrics` | full | refused | refused |

## Atomic admission

Whether a configured usage cap is genuinely enforced under concurrent ingest (one critical
section) or enforced *on average* (check-then-act, which a burst can outrun). An advisory
cap that reads as enforced is the failure this row exists to name.

| Backend | admission |
|---|---|
| sqlite | atomic — the cap holds |
| postgres | atomic — the cap holds |
| firestore | **advisory** — a concurrent burst can exceed the cap |
